items.title: Add burn-flex CPU backend (intended to replace burn-ndarray)
items.body:
## Summary

This PR lands **burn-flex**, a from-scratch pure-Rust CPU backend, as an additive backend alongside `burn-ndarray`. The long-term intent is for `burn-flex` to replace `burn-ndarray` as Burn's default CPU backend.

burn-flex was built and matured in a standalone repo ([antimora/burn-flex](https://github.com/antimora/burn-flex)) against the burn-backend-tests conformance suite, and this PR upstreams the crate plus all the wiring needed to use it through `burn-dispatch`, the `burn` umbrella crate, `burn-backend-tests`, `xtask`, and the release workflow.

## Why burn-flex?

`burn-ndarray` depends on the [ndarray](https://crates.io/crates/ndarray) crate, which has been slow to accept contributions and evolve. That limits how much Burn can tune its CPU backend. burn-flex is built directly on Burn's own native types (`Bytes`, `Shape`, `TensorData`, `Element`) from `burn-backend` and `burn-std`, so improvements go directly into Burn rather than waiting on an external crate.

### Performance vs burn-ndarray (Apple M3 Max)

#### Compute wins

burn-ndarray now uses macerator SIMD for f32 elementwise ops ([tracel-ai/burn#2851](https://github.com/tracel-ai/burn/pull/2851)), so contiguous f32 binary/unary ops are at parity. Flex's wins come from gemm, integer ops, fused kernels, and better tensor representation.

| Category          | Speedup      | Highlights                              |
| ----------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| Binary ops (f32)  | **~1x**      | Both use macerator SIMD                 |
| Binary ops (i32)  | **1.8-5.3x** | Flex uses i32, NdArray uses i64         |
| Matmul (square)   | **1.4-3.1x** | gemm at small/large sizes               |
| Matmul (batched)  | **1.3-2.2x** | Multi-head attention shapes             |
| Matmul (int)      | **3.7-6.5x** | gemm vs matrixmultiply for integers     |
| Conv2d (3x3)      | **1.1-3.7x** | Larger kernels and batches benefit most |
| Conv1d            | **4.3-9.8x** |                                         |
| Conv transpose    | **9.2-84x**  | Direct scatter vs im2col                |
| Attention         | **1.2-3.0x** | Fused softmax, 2-8x lower peak memory   |
| Pooling           | **1.1-3.1x** |                                         |
| Interpolation     | **1.1-6.3x** | Nearest 4-6x, bilinear 1.7-2.8x         |
| Reductions        | **1.3-5.4x** | Near-zero allocation for scalar results |
| Cumulative ops    | **2.1-95x**  | 1D cumsum: 95x faster                   |
| Gather/scatter    | **1.2-6.4x** |                                         |
| Unary (tanh, sin) | **1.3-2.0x** |                                         |
| Sort              | **2.3-29x**  | 2D sort up to 29x                       |
| Repeat dim        | **8.9-12x**  | Single alloc + memcpy vs N slice_assign |
| Tensor creation   | **16-33x**   | zeros/ones/full                         |
| Embedding         | **4.8-5.8x** |                                         |
| Quantize          | **1.3-1.5x** | Fused 2-pass implementation             |
| FFT (rfft/irfft)  | native       | Burn-flex ships an FFT implementation   |

#### Structural wins

These reflect better operation representation, not faster computation. burn-ndarray eagerly materializes data for these ops; burn-flex avoids the work entirely through zero-copy views and separated storage layouts.

| Category      | Improvement      | What changed                                                 |
| ------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Dequantize    | **122-238x**     | Direct `scale * x_q` vs reparsing `QuantizedBytes` each call |
| Quantized ops | **6.1-125x**     | Dominated by fast dequantize                                 |
| Slice/narrow  | **2.1-2,400x**   | Zero-copy strided view vs data copy                          |
| Unfold        | **920-130,000x** | O(1) strided view vs O(n) full materialization               |
| Expand        | **620-2,800x**   | Zero-copy broadcast (stride=0) vs data copy                  |
| Int cast      | **6.3-26,000x**  | Zero-copy reinterpret vs element-wise conversion             |

See `crates/burn-flex/BENCHMARKS.md` for the full per-op breakdown.

### Performance vs candle-core (pure-Rust, no BLAS)

Across 11 bench files covering every flex op that intersects with candle's CPU API, flex is as fast or faster on every operation category. Highlights: batched matmul 8-11x, conv1d 1.4-7.6x, softmax 1.4-1.7x, layer norm 1.6-3.4x, max/min reductions 3.8-5.1x.

## Feature highlights

- **Zero-copy layout ops**: `transpose`, `permute`, `flip`, `narrow`, `slice`, `unfold` (sliding windows as a strided view rather than materializing), `expand` (broadcast via zero strides)
- **Arc-based copy-on-write**: O(1) tensor cloning with automatic COW semantics; in-place mutation when uniquely owned
- **Convolutions**: unified 3D implementation with im2col + gemm. Conv1d/2d delegate to conv3d. Direct conv path for small spatial 1D convs (skips NHWC conversion and im2col). 1x1 pointwise fast path. Supports groups, dilation, padding
- **Attention**: auto-selects between two gemm-backed strategies based on sequence length. Short sequences use naive attention with two large gemm calls; larger shapes use tiled flash attention with online softmax for O(TILE_KV) memory per row. Both support causal masking, additive bias (ALiBi), softcap, custom scale, and cross-attention
- **Pooling**: max pool, avg pool, adaptive avg pool via unified 3D with backward pass support
- **Conv transpose**: scatter-based for upsampling
- **Portable SIMD via [macerator](https://crates.io/crates/macerator)**: automatic dispatch to NEON (aarch64), AVX2/AVX-512/SSE (x86_64), SIMD128 (wasm32), scalar fallback otherwise. No `#[cfg(target_arch)]` blocks anywhere in the crate
- **Matrix multiplication via [gemm](https://crates.io/crates/gemm)** with native f16 support. Strided batched matmul passes layout strides directly to gemm, so transposed views like `q.matmul(k.swap_dims(-2,-1))` run at contiguous speed with no copy
- **Native FFT**: Forward (rfft) and inverse (irfft) real FFT via Cooley-Tukey with complex packing, compile-time twiddle tables, SIMD butterflies, unrolled small kernels. Works in `no_std`
- **Quantization**: full quantize/dequantize support with per-tensor and per-block symmetric schemes. All ~40 quantized ops work out of the box. Layout ops on quantized tensors are zero-copy. Stores scales separately for direct `scale * x_q` dequantization instead of reparsing packed bytes
- **Dtype support**: f32, f64, f16 (native), bf16 (via f32 conversion), i8-i64, u8-u64
- **Parallel execution**: optional rayon for large tensors
- **Thread-safe by design**

## Correctness and portability

- All `burn-backend-tests` pass through `burn-dispatch` against the flex feature (1598 tests: 424 autodiff + 1174 tensor), and there are no regressions in the burn-ndarray path (1791 tests still pass)
- Burn's `burn-no-std-tests` integration suite passes (MNIST model inference in `#![no_std]`)
- Builds for embedded and WebAssembly targets: `thumbv6m-none-eabi` (ARM Cortex-M0+, no atomic pointers, via the `critical-section` feature), `thumbv7m-none-eabi`, `wasm32-unknown-unknown`
- Passes [Miri](https://github.com/rust-lang/miri) on all burn-flex code (validates memory safety of unsafe pointer arithmetic, bytemuck casts, and Send/Sync implementations)
- All ONNX model checks in `burn-onnx` pass
- Real model inference verified on ALBERT (masked LM) and MiniLM (sentence embeddings)

## Things worth flagging for review

1. **Phantom generic parameters on `Flex`**. burn-dispatch's macros expand `\$Backend<f32>` as a type alias, which doesn't work against a unit struct. Rather than diverge the macros, `Flex` now has phantom generic parameters: `pub struct Flex<E = f32, I = i32>`. The Backend impl stays non-generic so only `Flex<f32, i32>` is a Backend. Source-level compatibility is preserved (bare `Flex` resolves to `Flex<f32, i32>` via defaults). A compile-fail doctest locks this in. Making the impl truly generic over element types is a follow-up that would require rewriting the ops trait impls.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p burn-flex --lib` (501 pass)
- [x] `cargo test -p burn-flex --doc` (compile_fail guard for `Flex<f64, i64>: !Backend` passes)
- [x] `cargo test-flex` in `crates/burn-backend-tests` (1598 pass, 0 fail, 0 regressions)
- [x] `cargo test-ndarray` regression check (1791 pass, 0 regressions)
- [x] `cargo check -p burn-dispatch --no-default-features --features flex,std` clean
- [x] `cargo check -p burn-dispatch --no-default-features --features flex,ndarray,std` clean (both CPU backends coexist)
- [x] `cargo check -p burn-dispatch --no-default-features --features flex,std,autodiff` clean
- [x] `cargo check -p burn --no-default-features --features flex,std,autodiff,train` clean
- [x] `cargo check --workspace` clean across all examples

## Related

- Original standalone crate: https://github.com/antimora/burn-flex
- Detailed per-op comparison with burn-ndarray: `crates/burn-flex/COMPARISON.md`
- Architecture and memory strategy: `crates/burn-flex/ARCHITECTURE.md`
- Full benchmark numbers: `crates/burn-flex/BENCHMARKS.md`

items.title: Fix burn-flex attention rejecting broadcasted mask/bias
items.body:
### Related Issues/PRs

Fixes #4772.
Surfaces (and defers to) #4778 for a latent cubecl flash-attention bug - see "Latent cubecl bug exposed" below.

### Changes

`attention_naive` and `attention_flash` in `burn-flex` asserted strict shape equality between the optional mask/bias and the full `[batch, heads, seq_q, seq_kv]` attention shape, rejecting the ONNX Attention-23 broadcast forms (`[1, 1, seq_q, seq_kv]`, `[batch, 1, seq_q, seq_kv]`, etc.) that `burn-ndarray` handled cleanly. This regressed 11 `onnx-official-tests` attention cases after the burn-onnx migration to burn-flex - see issue #4772 for the full list.

Both the naive and flash paths now route optional mask/bias through a new `broadcast_attn_mask_bias` helper that:

1. Asserts the mask/bias is 4D (explicit up-front, so the error names the offending argument).
2. Delegates per-dim broadcast validation to `crate::ops::expand::expand`, which already panics when a source dim is neither equal to target nor `1`.
3. Materializes the resulting stride-0 view with `to_contiguous()` so the inner loops' precomputed `[batch_stride, head_stride]` offset math stays valid without teaching a broadcast-aware indexer.

The hot loops are untouched. `Option 2` from the issue (expand + materialize) was chosen over per-loop stride tracking to preserve the inner-loop simplicity, matching burn-flex's existing zero-copy broadcast idioms.

### Testing

Tests are split along their natural axis.

General ONNX broadcast equivalence tests live in `crates/burn-backend-tests/tests/tensor/float/module/attention.rs`, using the file's existing idiom (random `TestTensor<4>` compared against `attention_fallback::<TestBackend>` as the oracle, since the fallback's `B::float_add` / `B::float_mask_fill` already broadcast naturally). Three new cases:

- `test_attention_bias_broadcast_batch_and_heads` - `[1, 1, seq_len, seq_len]` bias
- `test_attention_bias_broadcast_heads_only` - `[num_batches, 1, seq_len, seq_len]` bias
- `test_attention_bool_mask_broadcast_batch_and_heads` - `[1, 1, seq_len, seq_len]` bool mask

burn-flex keeps the tests that can only be written in terms of its private internals:

- `test_flash_bias_broadcast_across_batch_and_heads` - calls `attention_flash` directly. The backend-tests cannot reach the flash branch because their shapes (`seq_len` up to 128) stay under `NAIVE_SCORE_BUDGET = 256K`, so the dispatcher always routes to naive.
- `test_mask_wrong_rank_panics` / `test_bias_incompatible_dim_panics` - `#[should_panic]` contract tests that lock in the helper's validation behavior (rank check, delegation to `expand`'s per-dim panic).

Run locally:

```
# burn-flex unit tests (574 pass, including the 3 flex-private broadcast tests)
cargo test -p burn-flex --lib

# general broadcast tests against burn-flex (13/13 attention tests pass)
cargo test -p burn-backend-tests --test tensor --no-default-features --features flex,std test_attention

# sanity check: same broadcast tests against ndarray backend (3/3 pass)
cargo test -p burn-backend-tests --test tensor --no-default-features --features ndarray,std attention_bias_broadcast
cargo test -p burn-backend-tests --test tensor --no-default-features --features ndarray,std attention_bool_mask_broadcast
```

### Latent cubecl bug exposed (#4778)

Initial CI runs on metal + f16 failed on `test_attention_bool_mask_broadcast_batch_and_heads`. Investigation showed this is a pre-existing cubecl flash-attention bug that my new test is the first to exercise, **not** a regression from this PR:

- **Fingerprint.** Output shape `[2, 3, 16, 32]` has strides `batch=1536, head=512, q=32`. Divergence starts at exactly **position 512 = (batch=0, head=1, q=0, col=0)**. Batch 0 head 0 matches `attention_fallback` perfectly; batch 0 head 1 onwards diverges. That's the unambiguous signature of a broadcast mask being applied to head 0 and not replicated to the remaining heads.
- **Magnitude.** Values at positions 513/514 disagree by 0.095 / 0.174 in absolute terms, with one side near zero - structural disagreement, not f16 precision noise.
- **Control.** The pre-existing `test_attention_all_options` uses the **identical** `Distribution::Uniform(0.,1.).greater_elem(0.7)` mask generator but at full shape `[num_batches, num_heads, seq_len, seq_len]` and passes on metal + f16. So the bug is specific to broadcast-shape handling, not to the mask values themselves.
- **Scope.** f32 passes; only f16 fails. The companion float-bias broadcast tests (`test_attention_bias_broadcast_*`) also pass on metal + f16, so the bug is specific to broadcast **bool masks**, not broadcast additive biases.
- **Not burn-flex.** burn-flex doesn't run on metal; metal goes through a separate cubecl/wgpu backend. My fix cannot have introduced this.

Filed as #4778 under the #4325 umbrella ("[burn-cubecl] FlashAttention doesn't work on most backends"). The bool-mask test is skipped on cubecl backends with f16 via `#[cfg(feature = "cube")]` plus a `TypeId` check, mirroring the existing `test_attention_no_mask` skip pattern in the same file. `cube` is a clean proxy for "cubecl backend in use" since only cuda/rocm/wgpu-family/cpu enable it, not flex/ndarray/tch. The `tensor_f16` test binary is already gated on `any(vulkan, cuda, rocm, metal)`, all of which transitively enable `cube`, so the cfg is a correct superset of every environment where the f16 attention test is compiled. Enable once #4778 is fixed.

### Checklist

- [x] Targeted tests pass (burn-flex lib + burn-backend-tests attention suite against both `flex` and `ndarray` features).
- [x] metal + f16 failure investigated, root cause isolated to a pre-existing cubecl broadcast-mask bug, filed as #4778, test skipped defensively on all cubecl backends with f16.

items.title: burn-flex: f16 follow-up to #4761 (enable tests, fix mean overflow, grid_sample f16, quantization)
items.body:
Follow-up to #4761. Enables the existing float test suite for burn-flex with `FloatElem = f16` and fixes the bugs that surface. Also brings SIMD to the half-precision mean path.

## Fixes

- **Reduction overflow**: `mean_dim` / `mean` for f16/bf16 materialised intermediate sums as f16 before dividing, clipping to inf when any slot summed above `f16::MAX = 65504`. Now fused on the f32 accumulator, narrowed only on store.
- **`grid_sample_2d`** was f32/f64 only. Replaced the macro with a generic impl so f16/bf16 route through the same f64 compute path.
- **Quantization**: `quantize()` read `qparams.scales` as `&[f32]` unconditionally. Switched to the existing `float_storage_as_f32` helper.
- **`q_matmul` default**: picked the dequantize target from device settings, which could mismatch the Float operand's dtype and panic in `float_matmul`. Now takes the target from whichever operand is `Float`.
- **Bogus I64 index asserts** in `int_gather`/`int_scatter_add`/`int_select`/`int_select_add` contradicted the kernels they called (`read_indices` already handles every integer dtype). Removing them also fixes ~28 unrelated int-path tests in the f32 debug suite.

items.title: Add contiguous reindexing for non-contiguous layer indices
items.body:
Problem

When PyTorch models use `nn.Sequential` with mixed layer types (e.g., Conv2d + ReLU), the state_dict keys have non-contiguous indices because only layers with parameters are saved:

```python
self.fc = nn.Sequential(
  nn.Conv2d(...),  # fc.0.weight, fc.0.bias
  nn.ReLU(),       # No parameters (index 1 skipped)
  nn.Conv2d(...),  # fc.2.weight, fc.2.bias
  nn.ReLU(),       # No parameters (index 3 skipped)
  nn.Conv2d(...),  # fc.4.weight, fc.4.bias
)
```

Burn models expect contiguous indices (fc.0, fc.1, fc.2), causing loading failures without manual remapping.

Solution

Added a reindex_contiguous() function that automatically remaps non-contiguous indices:
```
- fc.0.weight → fc.0.weight
- fc.2.weight → fc.1.weight
- fc.4.weight → fc.2.weight
```
 
API

```rust
// PytorchStore: contiguous_reindex is ON by default
let mut store = PytorchStore::from_file("model.pth");

// Disable if needed
let mut store = PytorchStore::from_file("model.pth")
    .contiguous_reindex(false);

// SafetensorsStore: contiguous_reindex is OFF by default
let mut store = SafetensorsStore::from_file("model.safetensors")
    .contiguous_reindex(true);  // Enable for PyTorch-exported safetensors
```

- [x] Confirmed that `cargo run-checks` command has been executed.
- [x] Made sure the book is up to date with changes in this PR.

### Changes

- Enable reindexing by default for `PytorchStore` (common use case), disable by default for `SafetensorsStore`
- Add `contiguous_reindex(bool)` builder method to both stores

items.title: Zero-copy tensor loading for NdArray backend
items.body: This PR implements true zero-copy tensor loading for the NdArray backend, addressing #4153 (discovered during #4154). Previously, even with zero-copy burnpack loading, the NdArray backend would copy all tensor data when creating ArcArray instances. This PR introduces NdArrayStorage, a copy-on-write storage type that can hold either borrowed (zero-copy) or owned data. ### Changes **Core Zero-Copy Infrastructure:** - New: `crates/burn-ndarray/src/storage.rs` - `NdArrayStorage` enum with `Borrowed` and `Owned` variants - Modified: `NdArrayTensor` now stores `NdArrayStorage` instead of `SharedArray` - Modified: `from_data()` attempts zero-copy loading first, falls back to copying if data is misaligned - Modified: Macros updated to convert storage to SharedArray for compatibility with existing operations **View-Based Optimizations (avoid COW for read-only operations):** - Global reductions: `sum_view`, `mean_view`, `prod_view`, `max_view`, `min_view` - Arg operations: `argmax_view`, `argmin_view` - Boolean reductions: `any_view`, `all_view` (with short-circuit evaluation) **Unnecessary Copy Elimination:** - `keepdim!` macro: reordered operations to avoid clones - `remainder()`: unified float/int paths using single `into_owned()` + Zip - `mask_fill()`: use `into_owned()` instead of `clone()` - `concatenate()`: reordered to avoid clone before reshape - `cumulative_with_op`: use `into_owned()` instead of `to_owned()` - `bool_into_int`: use `mapv` directly instead of intermediate Vec ### How it works 1. **Loading:** `NdArrayTensor::from_data()` checks if data bytes are properly aligned and creates `NdArrayStorage::Borrowed` when possible 2. **Reading:** Operations use `.view()` for zero-copy access to borrowed data 3. **Writing:** Operations that mutate call `.into_shared()` which triggers copy-on-write (copies only if borrowed) 4. **Compatibility:** Existing operations work unchanged via macro conversion **For borrowed (zero-copy) storage:** 1. Load tensor → Borrowed storage (points to static/mmap'd memory) 2. Call operation (e.g., `exp()`) 3. COW triggers → Copy data to new owned buffer 4. Write results in-place to that buffer 5. Return owned buffer **For already-owned storage (SharedArray with Arc):** 1. Tensor has owned SharedArray (`Arc`) 2. Call operation (e.g., `exp()`) 3. If Arc refcount == 1 → Write in-place, no copy! 4. If Arc refcount > 1 → Clone first, then write in-place 5. Return the buffer ### Benchmark Results Loading 312.2 MB Model to NdArray Backend (CPU) | Mode | Time | Allocations | Speedup | |------------------|----------|-------------|----------------------------------| | file_copy | 31.7 ms | 654.7 MB | baseline | | file_zero_copy | 106.7 µs | 97.2 KB | 297x faster, 6,700x less memory | | static_copy | 22.2 ms | 1.309 GB | baseline | | static_zero_copy | 65.5 µs | 97.06 KB | 339x faster, 13,800x less memory | The remaining ~97 KB allocation is metadata only (shapes, enum wrappers, Arc overhead) - tensor data is truly zero-copy. ### Test Plan - All existing burn-ndarray tests pass (28 tests) - New storage unit tests added and passing - Benchmark validates zero-copy behavior ### Breaking Changes None. The API remains unchanged - `NdArrayTensor::from_data()` works exactly as before, but now automatically uses zero-copy when possible. ### Related Issues - Closes #4153 - Follow-up to #4154 - #2871 - To minimize memory usage even further #4183 ### Real model testing Tested on CLIP ViT-B-32-vision Burn Model for ndarray backend and state embedding into static region. Made sure the accuracy remains. Along the way had to fix `into_vec_unchecked` for alignment handling with embedded binary data.

items.title: Fix MPS "Placeholder storage has not been allocated" error for embedding operations
items.body:
Adds a workaround for the 'Placeholder storage has not been allocated' error on MPS devices by performing embedding and embedding_backward operations on CPU and transferring results back to MPS. This addresses issues with lazy allocation in PyTorch MPS backend.

## Pull Request Template

### Checklist

- [x] Confirmed that `cargo run-checks` command has been executed.
- [x] Made sure the book is up to date with changes in this PR.

### Related Issues/PRs

Fixes https://github.com/tracel-ai/burn/issues/4038

### Changes
#### Problem

When using the tch backend with MPS device (Apple Silicon), embedding operations crash with:

RuntimeError: Placeholder storage has not been allocated on MPS device!
Exception raised from Placeholder at aten/src/ATen/native/mps/OperationUtils.mm:522

This affects both forward (embedding) and backward (embedding_backward) passes, making it impossible to train any model using embeddings on
MPS.

#### Root Cause

This is an upstream PyTorch bug where MPS uses lazy tensor allocation, but the index_select operation (used internally by embedding) attempts to use tensors before their storage has been materialized on the MPS device.

Upstream issues:
- https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/123995 - torch.embedding, Linear and others raise this error
- https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/130790 - Training on M1 MBP (closed as "not planned")
- https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/149184 - Still open as of March 2025

Related Burn issue:
- https://github.com/tracel-ai/burn/issues/4038

#### Attempted Fixes

1. Dummy forward pass during initialization - Attempted to force allocation by running a dummy embedding lookup during model init. Did not work.
2. Calling .contiguous() - Attempted to force tensor materialization by calling .contiguous() on weights and indices before embedding. Did not work.
3. CPU roundtrip (this PR) - Route embedding operations through CPU when on MPS device, then transfer results back. This works.

#### Solution

When the input tensors are on MPS device, we:
1. Transfer weights and indices to CPU
2. Perform the embedding operation on CPU
3. Transfer the result back to MPS

This bypasses the buggy MPS index_select implementation entirely.

```rust
if matches!(weights.tensor.device(), tch::Device::Mps) {
    let cpu_weights = weights.tensor.to(tch::Device::Cpu);
    let cpu_indices = indices.tensor.to(tch::Device::Cpu);
    let result = tch::Tensor::embedding(&cpu_weights, &cpu_indices, -1, false, false)
        .to(tch::Device::Mps);
    return TchTensor::new(result);
}
```

The same pattern is applied to embedding_backward.

Performance Trade-off

This fix introduces CPU↔MPS data transfers for embedding operations. However:
- Embedding lookups are typically small relative to the rest of model computation
- The alternative is a crash, so this makes MPS actually usable
- All other MPS-accelerated operations (matmul, activations, convolutions, etc.) continue to run on GPU
- When PyTorch fixes the upstream bug, this workaround can be removed

### Testing

Tested with https://github.com/GregorLueg/node2vec-rs which uses a Skip-Gram model with embeddings:

cargo run --release --no-default-features --features tch-mps -- --input tests/data/karate.csv

Before fix: Crashes immediately on first embedding forward pass
After fix: Completes all 5 training epochs successfully

items.title: Add float cast op for JIT backend
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] Confirmed that `run-checks all` script has been executed.
- [x] Made sure the book is up to date with changes in this PR.

### Related Issues/PRs

Follow-up of #2483

### Changes

Added `float_cast` implementation for `burn-jit`, `burn-fusion` and `burn-router`.

- Removed elem type generic from `JitTensor`
  - `JitTensor` now contains the dtype field
  - Refactored all calls with generics to have the correct generic types propagation (new `execute_with_dtype` macro to call cubecl kernels)
- Added `Primitive` trait for backend tensor primitives
  - Motivation: all primitives previously had the same trait requirements, and now we need to report the correct dtype in the `Display` implementation for `Tensor` (`K::elem_type_name()` would report the default floating point dtype even for tensors cast to another precision)
- Added dtype checks for binary float ops (no automatic type promotion for now, so we panic for different types)

**Known issue**
Trying to concatenate tensors cast to a different floating point dtype will fail with the current `cat_with_slice_assign` implementation because the output tensor is initialized with the default floating point element precision in `K::empty(...)`.

```rust
let tensor1: Tensor<B, 2> = Tensor::from_floats([[2., 3.], [4., 5.]], &device).cast(DType::F16);
let tensor2 = Tensor::ones_like(&tensor1).cast(DType::F16);
let tensor3 = Tensor::zeros_like(&tensor1).cast(DType::F16);

// Panics with incompatible dtype (for output)
let output = Tensor::<B, 2>::cat(vec![tensor1, tensor2, tensor3], 0);
```

**TODO**
- [ ] Implement `float_cast` for ndarray
- [ ] Remove redundant precision bridge

### Testing

Added new tests for primitive trait.

There had been a misconception about contiguous load in the previous version. Each thread was loading n contiguous entries, when in fact it should be the n different threads that load n contiguous entries.
